subject: Bridgework SDK implementation & cutover coordination
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmepay.com>, procurement@acmepay.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Bridgework SDK implementation & cutover coordination

Hi Sanjay / Acme procurement team,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — great to see how you're using LLMs as part of the payments fraud workflow. Per our conversation, attaching an onboarding checklist and a short mutual action plan to get you from sandbox -> production with Redwood Dedicated capacity.

High-level asks from our side so we can create the cutover runbook:
- Confirm the production cutover window you prefer (UTC windows work best for us; suggested: Sat 2028-05-06 02:00–06:00 UTC).
- Provide the current LLM endpoint(s) you call today and an estimate of peak qps during the cutover and steady-state.
- Confirm who will own key rotation and where you store API keys (HashiVault / AWS Secrets Manager / other).
- Share any IP allowlists or VPC peering gating we should add ahead of time.

Notes on what we attach:
- bridgework-onboarding-checklist.xlsx — detailed step-by-step (API keys, IPs, test vectors, rollback criteria).
- We'll also publish a small SDK sample bundle with retry/backoff defaults and a preferred header schema.

Typical Redwood suggestions (we'll finalize with SE):
- Use short client-side timeouts for initial calls (2–3s) and switch to server streaming for longer-generation paths.
- Start with conservative batch sizes to measure tail-latency; increase batching only once SLOs are stable.
- Respect 429/503 by honoring Retry-After and backing off with jitter.

I'll loop in Monica from CSM to manage the MAP and Vivek (solutions) for the technical run. Can you confirm the cutover window and share the produce endpoints by EOD Friday?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

Attachment: bridgework-onboarding-checklist.xlsx

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmepay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmepay.com, Marta Iglesias <marta.iglesias@clearpay.es>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Bridgework SDK implementation & cutover coordination

Laura — thanks, received. A few quick answers and questions from our side:

Answers:
- Production endpoints: currently we proxy to internal host api.acmepay.internal/v1/llm (single endpoint that fans out).
- Peak qps during daytime: ~45 qps; peak sustained for short bursts ~120 qps (we can throttle upstream).
- API keys: stored in HashiCorp Vault; rotation is quarterly, procurement will own the rotation timeline.
- Network: we can provide allowlist IPs; we prefer peering but will accept IP allowlists for initial cutover.

Questions/concerns:
1) Endpoint migration: we want to do a dual-write pattern for 48h — send requests to both current endpoint and Redwood sandbox, compare scores and latency. Any gotchas?
2) Retries: our current client retries 3 times with fixed 500ms backoff — we've seen duplicate-cost issues with retries. What's your recommendation?
3) Rate limits: If Redwood returns 429, do you have a recommended max qps per token class?

Also procurement asked for an SOW-level doc for internal approval; if you can share the MAP PDF we can attach it to the internal ticket.

Regards,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering | AcmePay
sanjay@acmepay.com

Hi Sanjay / Acme team — looping in CS and Solutions to own the cutover and tech validation.

High-level MAP we usually follow (short):
- Phase 0 (Sandbox smoke): 48–72h dual-write + validation vectors (we'll provide a test vector set).
- Phase 1 (Pilot): 1 week, small traffic slice (5–10% production qps). Confirm observability hooks.
- Phase 2 (Cutover): agreed maintenance window; staged increase to 100% over 2h with rollback checkpoints.

Owner matrix:
- Redwood CSM: Monica Patel — MAP, runbook approvals, escalation contact.
- Redwood SE: Vivek Kulkarni — technical run, SDK samples, retries/timeouts, custom headers.
- Acme: Sanjay Rao + Platform Eng — key rotation ownership, final IP allowlists.

I've attached a short MAP (MVP-cutover-MAP.pdf) you can use for procurement. We'll also add the MAP to the HubSpot record HS-ACME-452.

Action items for this week:
- Sanjay: confirm sample traffic for sandbox (range and peak bursts).
- Vivek: share SDK samples and recommended retry/timeouts by tomorrow EOB PT.
- Laura: confirm contract anchor (SLA and billing cadence) for procurement.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: MVP-cutover-MAP.pdf

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmepay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2028 09:16:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Bridgework SDK implementation & cutover coordination — SDK & runbook details

All — this looks good. Confirming the proposed cutover window: Sat 2028-05-06 02:00–06:00 UTC is acceptable.

We will:
- Enable dual-write to sandbox.redwood.ai starting 2028-04-24 00:00 UTC for 72h.
- Provide a 2-hour pilot slice (10% traffic) on 2028-05-04 for observability tuning.
- Share HashiCorp Vault access policy for the Redwood integration by 2028-04-21 EOD (we're on it).

One last ask: can you add a quick post-cutover monitoring runbook with escalation numbers (Pager/Slack + email) and a rollback checklist? Procurement wants that in the SOW.

I'll attach the procurement ticket once Monica sends the MAP. Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. Looking forward to the pre-cutover test.

Regards,
Sanjay
Head of Platform Engineering | AcmePay
